newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DISPUTED FRENCH CUP MATCH TO BE PLAYED ON NEUTRAL GROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DISPUTED FRENCH CUP MATCH TO BE PLAYED ON NEUTRAL GROUND.

text.p: A disputed French Cup first round match between Marseille and Lille, postponed after a legal battle between the two sides, will be held on neutral ground next month.
Officials from Marseille and Lille met at the French Soccer Federation (FFF) on Tuesday and agreed on a compromise. The tie will now take place in Valence, in central France, on February 4.
"We have finally come to an agreement. I want to thank both sides. We have decided to put an end to all the legal and sports proceedings that had been started," said FFF president Claude Simonet.

Both teams claimed they should host the match, Marseille saying they had been drawn first, Lille arguing that Marseille's pitch could not be used because of works being carried out ahead of the 1998 World Cup.

Because of the works, the FFF first decided to hold the match in Lille but Marseille appealed to soccer authorities, and to the national Olympic committee before a civil court eventually decided to postpone any decision for a month.
"We cannot say we are happy with the outcome but this case had to stop. Let's hope the match will be even more hard-fought," said Marseille president Jean-Michel Roussier.
He, however, claimed once more that Marseille could have hosted the game: "We're entertaining Bastia in the league on Saturday in front of an attendance of 20,000," he said.
Lille president Bernard Lecomte said he was worried that teams could be tempted to turn to civil courts from now on.

"In a week of negotiations, we discovered that the decisions of sports powers could be contested. It poses a real problem. Who knows whether one day someone will not contest the decision of a referee in court ?" he warned.
